findings.reason: parser.ts:1452 only does state.position++, while the removed skipByteOrderMark also set lineStart. So blockIndent at :1243 is 1, readBlockMapping exits at :1131 when line 2 has lineIndent 0, and readDocument throws at :1422. hasSeparation at :336 is also false after the BOM, so a '# comment' right after the BOM is not skipped. The only BOM test (load-other.test.mjs:7) has a single key, so it misses this.
findings.claim: The leading BOM is now skipped without setting lineStart, so the first line's column is off by one. A BOM-prefixed file with more than one top-level key, or with a leading comment or '...' marker, now fails to parse or parses wrongly.
findings.evidence: The new line `if (state.input.charCodeAt(state.position) === 0xFEFF) state.position++` replaces `skipByteOrderMark`, which also ran `state.lineStart = state.position`. In `parseNode`, `const blockIndent = state.position - state.lineStart` (line 1243) is now 1 for the first node. `readBlockMapping` is therefore opened with nodeIndent 1. On line 2, `lineIndent` is 0, so `else if (state.lineIndent < nodeIndent) break` (line 1131) ends the mapping after one entry. `readDocument` then throws 'end of the stream or a document separator is expected' (line 1422) because `b` is not a separator. `skipSeparationSpace`'s `hasSeparation = state.position === state.lineStart || ...` (line 336) is also false after the BOM, so `﻿# c` is not read as a comment. The only BOM unit test, `load('﻿foo: bar\n')` in test/core/units/load-other.test.mjs, has a single key and does not hit this.

findings.reason: The new checks at :672, :776 and :1421 only match testDocumentSeparator exactly at lineStart. The BOM skip at :1452 runs only once, before the stream loop, where skipByteOrderMark used to run before every document. So in 'foo\n﻿---\nbar' the BOM stays at lineStart, the '---' is never matched, and the scalar continues into the next document. Both reviewers traced the same input to the same merged result.
findings.claim: With testDocumentBoundary removed, a BOM before a later document's '---' or '%' is no longer seen as a document boundary. Plain-scalar documents silently merge into one value, and other documents throw.
findings.evidence:
Old code: `testDocumentBoundary` skipped a BOM at line start and treated a following `---` or `%` as a boundary, and the stream loop called `skipByteOrderMark` before each document. New code: `state.position === state.lineStart && testDocumentSeparator(state)` only matches `-`/`.` at the exact line start, and the BOM skip only runs at position 0 (line 1452). Trace for `foo
﻿---
bar
`: in `readPlainScalar`, the EOL branch continues because `lineIndent >= nodeIndent`. The BOM is not whitespace and is not in `PATTERN_NON_PRINTABLE` (line 24), so `end` moves past it. The following `---` is no longer at `lineStart`, so the check at line 776 never fires and `loadAll` returns one scalar `'foo ﻿--- bar'` instead of two documents. For a mapping document, the end-of-document check at line 1421 throws instead. The same applies to block scalars at line 672.
